findings.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — [P1/100] `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass` leaves every stateful abstract operation unimplemented, so `MetricAlertFire.detector_handler` can no longer be instantiated by `Detector.detector_handler` and the registered metric-alert detector has no viable integration path.

[P2/75] src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:128 — Changing `) -> dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]:` replaces the established list-returning `DetectorHandler.evaluate` contract while adding the occurrence hook, so a non-stateful handler that still returns its prior list causes `process_detectors` to call `.values()` on that list and fail, an unaccepted behavior change beyond “Add in hook for producing occurrences from the stateful detector.”

[P1/100] src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):` now inherits the unimplemented abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` methods, so constructing the registered `metric_alert_fire` handler raises `TypeError` and aborts processing whenever that detector type is used.

[P2/75] src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:60 — `for result in detector_results.values():` performs one synchronous Kafka publish for every group key with no batch or cap, so a single high-cardinality packet can exhaust the worker time budget after partial publishing and then retry the already-published prefix.

src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:126 — [P2/75] Changing the base handler contract to `"-> dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]"` is unrelated to adding an occurrence-production hook and forces every existing non-stateful handler and caller to migrate from the established list API, expanding the change beyond the stated intent.

src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — [P1/75] Replacing the inert metric-alert placeholder with `"class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass"` is unrelated to the hook and makes this registered handler abstract, so processing a `metric_alert_fire` detector now fails while constructing its handler instead of safely returning no evaluations.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the abstract base class DetectorHandler.evaluate() is changed to return dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult] (line 125-127). The MockDetectorHandler in tests is also updated to return a dict (line 61-63: 'return {None: DetectorEvaluationResult(None, True, DetectorPriorityLevel.HIGH)}'). The finding claims non-stateful handlers still return lists, but the diff shows the abstract method signature was changed and the test mock was updated accordingly. adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1/100] src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — `class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]):` now inherits the unimplemented abstract `counter_names`, `get_dedupe_value`, `get_group_key_values`, and `build_occurrence_and_event_data` methods, so constructing the registered `metric_alert_fire` handler raises `TypeError` and aborts processing whenever that detector type is used.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows MetricAlertDetectorHandler changing from DetectorHandler to StatefulDetectorHandler with just 'pass' as its body. Looking at StatefulDetectorHandler in the diff, it has multiple @abc.abstractmethod decorators: get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. The counter_names is also referenced in the test's MockDetectorStateHandler. Since MetricAlertDetectorHandler only has 'pass' and doesn't implement these abstract methods, instantiating it would raise TypeError at runtime. This is a real bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1/100] src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:62 — `create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result)` publishes the occurrence before the later `handler.commit_state_updates()`, so a database/Redis commit failure after a successful Kafka write leaves the transition unrecorded and a retry emits the same alert again.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows that in process_detectors(), create_issue_occurrence_from_result(result) is called at line 62 for each result, which publishes to Kafka. However, handler.commit_state_updates() is not called within process_detectors() - looking at the diff, there's no commit_state_updates() call after the evaluate loop. The StatefulDetectorHandler.evaluate() method enqueues state updates via enqueue_state_update() (line 287), but these are only committed when commit_state_updates() is explicitly called. If the Kafka write succeeds but a subsequent failure occurs before state is committed, the detector state won't reflect the transition, potentially causing duplicate alerts on retry. This is a valid atomicity concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P2/75] src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:60 — `for result in detector_results.values():` performs one synchronous Kafka publish for every group key with no batch or cap, so a single high-cardinality packet can exhaust the worker time budget after partial publishing and then retry the already-published prefix.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that the loop at line 60 iterates over detector_results.values() and calls create_issue_occurrence_from_result() for each result, which publishes to Kafka synchronously. This is visible in the diff. However, this is not a new bug introduced by this diff - the previous code also had the same loop structure (lines 56-72 in the old code show similar iteration). The diff changes the data structure from list to dict but maintains the same synchronous publishing pattern. The concern about high-cardinality packets causing issues is a valid architectural concern, but it's pre-existing behavior, not introduced by this diff. This is an important observation about the code's scalability limitations that the diff doesn't address, making it an important_non_bug rather than a bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/detector.py:126 — [P2/75] Changing the base handler contract to `"-> dict[DetectorGroupKey, DetectorEvaluationResult]"` is unrelated to adding an occurrence-production hook and forces every existing non-stateful handler and caller to migrate from the established list API, expanding the change beyond the stated intent.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims the change 'forces every existing non-stateful handler and caller to migrate from the established list API'. However, looking at the diff, the only non-stateful handler shown is MockDetectorHandler in the test file, which is also updated to return a dict. The MetricAlertDetectorHandler now extends StatefulDetectorHandler and uses 'pass' (inheriting the dict-returning evaluate). The change is consistent across the codebase shown - both the abstract method signature and all implementations are updated together. This is a coordinated API change, not an incomplete migration that breaks existing code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/incidents/grouptype.py:11 — [P1/75] Replacing the inert metric-alert placeholder with `"class MetricAlertDetectorHandler(StatefulDetectorHandler[QuerySubscriptionUpdate]): pass"` is unrelated to the hook and makes this registered handler abstract, so processing a `metric_alert_fire` detector now fails while constructing its handler instead of safely returning no evaluations.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims that MetricAlertDetectorHandler becomes abstract and will fail when constructing its handler. However, looking at the diff, StatefulDetectorHandler is not abstract - it has concrete implementations of evaluate() and other methods. The class inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler which has a concrete evaluate() method (lines 225-245 in the diff show the evaluate method implementation). The only abstract methods in StatefulDetectorHandler are get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data. While MetricAlertDetectorHandler doesn't implement these, this was already the case before (the old evaluate() just returned an empty list with a TODO comment). The change doesn't make the handler more broken than it was - it was already a placeholder that needed implementation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [P1/100] tests/sentry/workflow_engine/processors/test_detector.py:536 — `build_mock_occurrence_and_event(handler, "val1", 6, PriorityLevel.HIGH)` creates an expected occurrence fingerprint for `val1`, while the invocation at line 548 evaluates `"group_key"`, so the changed `test_dedupe` assertion deterministically compares unequal occurrence fingerprints and fails.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the test_dedupe method in TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue (lines 530-548), the test calls build_mock_occurrence_and_event with group_key='val1' at line 536, but then calls handler.evaluate_group_key_value with group_key='group_key' at line 548. The build_mock_occurrence_and_event function uses handler.build_fingerprint(group_key) to create the fingerprint, so the expected_result will have a fingerprint based on 'val1' while the actual result from evaluate_group_key_value will have a fingerprint based on 'group_key'. This mismatch means the test assertion will fail because the occurrence fingerprints won't match.
